topic: Vitamins and deficiency diseases — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The vitamin whose deficiency causes scurvy — bleeding gums and slow wound healing — is:
questions.explanation: Scurvy — caused by deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) — was the classic scourge of long sea voyages (British sailors were called 'limeys' for the citrus fruits they were made to eat). Amla, guava, citrus fruits, chillies are rich sources. Vitamin C is also a cofactor for collagen synthesis and enhances iron absorption.

questions.stem: Rickets — weak and deformed bones in children — is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is crucial for calcium absorption; its deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults. Called the 'sunshine vitamin' — the skin synthesises it on exposure to UV-B sunlight. Also found in fatty fish, egg yolk, fortified milk. South-Asians with dark skin living indoors or in less-sunny regions often have low levels even today.

questions.stem: Match the vitamin with its deficiency disease. A. Vitamin A. B. Vitamin B1. C. Vitamin B12. D. Vitamin K. List-II: 1. Night blindness, 2. Beri-beri, 3. Pernicious anaemia, 4. Poor blood clotting.
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) — night blindness, xerophthalmia. Vitamin B1 (thiamine) — beri-beri (leg weakness, heart problems). Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) — pernicious anaemia (memory issues too; only animal sources — vegans need supplements). Vitamin K — poor blood clotting, haemorrhages; the only vitamin synthesised by gut bacteria in usable amounts.

questions.stem: The group of fat-soluble vitamins comprises:
questions.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins — A, D, E, K — stored in the liver and fatty tissue; excess can accumulate (hypervitaminosis). Water-soluble — C and the B-complex (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9, B12); not stored in large amounts, so they need continual intake, but overdose is rarely harmful because excess is excreted. Mnemonic — 'ADEK' stays; the rest washes out.

questions.stem: Pellagra — characterised by the 3Ds (dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia) — is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Pellagra — caused by chronic niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency. Classically seen in populations with a maize-heavy diet (niacin in corn is bound and unavailable unless the corn is treated with lime — nixtamalisation — as is traditional in Mesoamerica). The name comes from Italian 'pelle agra' (rough skin). B9 deficiency — megaloblastic anaemia and neural-tube defects in the foetus.

questions.explanation: Iron is essential for haemoglobin; its deficiency is the commonest cause of anaemia, particularly in Indian women and children. Symptoms — fatigue, pallor, shortness of breath. Good dietary sources — leafy greens, jaggery, red meat, iron-fortified foods. Goitre — iodine deficiency; rickets — Vitamin D; scurvy — Vitamin C.

questions.stem: The only vitamin the human skin can synthesise on exposure to sunlight is:
questions.explanation: UV-B light converts a precursor (7-dehydrocholesterol) in the skin to Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol). Further conversion in the liver and kidneys produces the active hormone calcitriol. Daily sun exposure of 15-30 minutes (face, arms) is usually enough in tropical latitudes. Darker skin and heavy sunscreen use reduce synthesis.
